kernels.l1: One hoop shared out across two others gives the same shading either way.
kernels.l2: When you overlap one hoop with two hoops joined together, you can do it one hoop at a time and join the answers. The shading comes out the same.
kernels.l3: Meeting one collection against a pooled pair gives the same result as meeting it against each and then pooling. Both operations spread across each other this way, which is more than arithmetic manages.
kernels.l4: Each of union and intersection distributes over the other. Unlike arithmetic, where only multiplication distributes over addition, here the two operations distribute both ways.
kernels.l5: Both distributive laws hold for sets, each proved by double inclusion with a case split in one direction; the symmetry has no arithmetic analogue.
kernels.l6: Intersection and union each distribute over the other, which arithmetic never manages — only multiplication distributes over addition. The two laws are duals: complement one, apply De Morgan, and the other drops out.
kernels.l7: Intersection distributes over union and union distributes over intersection; the two laws are De Morgan duals, and that mutual symmetry has no counterpart in the arithmetic of + and ×.
kernels.l8: Each of union and intersection spreads across the other, which is a stronger symmetry than arithmetic has: multiplication spreads across addition, but addition does not spread across multiplication.
